endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: turner_bend_private_fee_landing_anchor turner-bend-private-fee-landing-area: Turner Bend’s operator identifies its landing at the Highway 23 / Mulberry River corridor and describes it as load/unload access for private boaters subject to an access wristband, parking permission, and shuttle/loading rules. The route coordinate is a bridge-corridor/access-area anchor, not a surveyed landing toe; access is conditional on current operator terms and fees.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the named authoritative access-area control (turner_bend_private_fee_landing_anchor turner-bend-private-fee-landing-area) on Mulberry River; this confirms the public access site, not the exact water-edge point. Confirm the water-edge location and carry before paddling.

endpoints.coordinateEvidenceDetail: ar_usfs_redding_mulberry_access_20260919 redding-recreation-area-mulberry-canoe-launch: Recreation.gov identifies Redding Campground on the Mulberry River in the Ozark-St. Francis National Forests. The official Mulberry River Wild and Scenic River plan states the campground is adjacent to a Mulberry River access point, and Forest Service recreation schedules list Redding day-use/launch access. Retain the stored route point as a conditional campground/rock-canoe-launch anchor; the 347-foot named-flowline offset reflects the campground, parking, trail, and shoreline facility footprint rather than a wrong endpoint.
endpoints.note: Stored coordinate matches the named authoritative access-area control (ar_usfs_redding_mulberry_access_20260919 redding-recreation-area-mulberry-canoe-launch) on Mulberry River; access is conditional (Confirm current Forest Service campground/day-use status, fee, parking, launch condition, river level, and any seasonal or local restrictions before use.), not unrestricted public access. This confirms the managed access area, not the exact water-edge point.
